title: Cross-study TE-diversity reference (Wang et al. 2025)
legend: Panels a and c show genome size against top-ten-superfamily Shannon entropy and the Gini-Simpson index for 11 published salamanders and 21 current Desmognathus species. Panels b and d show the exact published vertebrate-group distributions beside all 34 current Desmognathus summaries. Wang et al. values come from RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker; current values come from dnaPipeTE. The comparison is descriptive and has no pooled fit. Descriptive cross-study context only; no pooled regression or hypothesis test is shown. Wang et al. 2025 published top-10 TE-superfamily indices are exact CC0-1.0 Dryad values (dataset DOI 10.5061/dryad.zpc866tkv; article DOI 10.1038/s42003-025-08127-3) produced from RepeatModeler/RepeatMasker annotations. Current top-10 indices are reclosed calculations from dnaPipeTE compositions. The pipelines are different and not method-harmonized. Current genome sizes are D. fuscus assembly-anchored estimates, not direct species C-values.
alt_text: Two scatterplots compare genome size with top-ten-superfamily Shannon and Gini-Simpson diversity for published salamanders and current Desmognathus. Two aligned box-and-point panels compare nine vertebrate groups, highlighting published salamanders in blue and current Desmognathus in orange. No regression line or p-value is shown.
